The question is that the amendments on sheet 3908 be agreed to. _One Nation's circulated amendments—_ (1) Schedule 1, item 13, page 11 (line 30), omit paragraph 227A(4)(h). Sue Lines The question is that the remaining stages of the bill be agreed to and the bill be now passed.

Daniel Mulino I move: That the amendments be agreed to. The bill establishes External Reporting Australia, or ERA, Australia's new body responsible for the development and maintenance of accounting auditing and assurance standards. In recent years, we've seen behaviour from large accounting, auditing and consulting firms in Australia that is not fair or honest. This bill represents a major development in the setting and maintenance of standards. The amendments on which we seek the House's concurrence are all consistent with the policy intent of the bill. I commend the bill to the House. Tony Burke I move that the question be put. Milton Dick The question is that the question be put.
Milton Dick The question is that the amendments be agreed to.

Referred Appropriation Bills No.3 and No.4 2025-2026 and the Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill No.2 2025-2026 to the Federation Chamber immediately, with two other bills to follow the adjournment of their second-reading debates.

Argued that the Treasury Laws Amendment (Financial Reporting System Reform) Bill 2026 would abolish three established standard-setting bodies and replace them with External Reporting Australia, concentrating authority and risking independence. Opposed the bill in its current form and sought Senate Economics Legislation Committee scrutiny, while identifying insurance affordability and financial advice as more immediate priorities.

Argued that the Treasury Laws Amendment (Financial Reporting System Reform) Bill 2026 would establish External Reporting Australia by combining standard-setting functions of three existing bodies, preserve existing standards, strengthen accountability and support accounting, auditing, assurance and sustainability standards; the question remained unresolved.

Moved changes to committee memberships, appointing substitute and participating members for inquiries into private health consumers, financial reporting reform and coal mining industry long service leave; the question was agreed to.

Opposed replacing the Financial Reporting Council, Australian Accounting Standards Board and Auditing and Assurance Standards Board with External Reporting Australia, arguing that the case for change had not been made and the new minister-appointed body could politicise independent accounting standards. Raised concerns that environmental, social and governance reporting could discourage domestic industrial production.

Spoke against the Treasury Laws Amendment (Financial Reporting System Reform) Bill 2026, arguing that replacing the Financial Reporting Council, Australian Accounting Standards Board and Auditing and Assurance Standards Board with External Reporting Australia removes important structural separation without a demonstrated governance failure.

Considered the Treasury Laws Amendment (Financial Reporting System Reform) Bill 2026, agreeing to a second reading amendment and putting committee amendments from the Australian Greens and One Nation concerning ethics, accounting and sustainability standards, eligibility for governing and standard-setting bodies, and New Zealand representation before the bill's remaining stages were agreed to.
